'''Peter John Olver''' (11 January 1952, [[Twickenham]]) is a British-American mathematician working in [[differential geometry]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Peter Olver {{!}} AMAAZE|url=https://amaaze.umn.edu/peter-olver|access-date=2021-11-28|website=amaaze.umn.edu}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
After moving to the USA in 1961, Olver obtained a bachelor's degree in Applied Mathematics at [[Brown University]] in 1973 and a PhD in Mathematics at [[Harvard University]] in 1976. His PhD thesis was entitled "''Symmetry Groups of Partial Differential Equations"'' and was written under the supervision of [[Garrett Birkhoff]].<ref name="MGP">{{MathGenealogy|id=11330|title=Peter Olver}}</ref>

He worked as a [[Leonard Eugene Dickson|L.E. Dickson]] Instructor in Mathematics at [[University of Chicago]] (1976-1978) and as a research fellow at [[University of Oxford]] (1978-1980). He then moved to [[University of Minnesota]] as assistant professor, and he became full professor in the same university in 1985. Between 1992 and 1993 he was professor at [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web|author=Peter J. Olver|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=http://www.math.umn.edu/~olver/cv.pdf|access-date=19 June 2017}}</ref>

Olver was member of the board of directors of [[Foundations of Computational Mathematics]] from 2002 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=FoCM • Foundations of Computational Mathematics • Governance|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_before_2008.php|access-date=2021-11-28|website=focm-society.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=FoCM • Foundations of Computational Mathematics • Governance|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_2008-2011.php|access-date=2021-11-28|website=focm-society.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=FoCM • Foundations of Computational Mathematics • Governance|url=http://focm-society.org/governance_2011-2014.php|access-date=2021-11-28|website=focm-society.org}}</ref> He was elected fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013<ref>{{cite web|author=AMS|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|access-date=19 June 2017|archive-date=25 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> and of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2014, for "''developing new geometric methods for differential equations leading to applications in fluid mechanics, elasticity, quantum mechanics, and image processing''."<ref>{{Cite web|title=SIAM > Prizes & Recognition > Fellows Program > All SIAM Fellows > Class of 2014|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/fellows-program/all-siam-fellows/class-of-2014|access-date=2021-11-28|website=www.siam.org}}</ref> Olver is also member of [[International Society for the Interaction of Mechanics and Mathematics]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=ISIMM Home Page|url=https://isimm.unipg.it/|access-date=2021-11-28|website=isimm.unipg.it|archive-date=2022-02-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203165748/http://isimm.unipg.it/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and an elected fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name="CV" />

== Research ==
Olver's primary research fields are [[differential geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]]. His main interests involve the application of [[Lie group]]s and [[symmetry group|symmetries]] to the geometry of [[differential equation]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Olver|first=Peter J.|date=1977-06-01|title=Evolution equations possessing infinitely many symmetries|journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume=18|issue=6|pages=1212–1215|doi=10.1063/1.523393|bibcode=1977JMP....18.1212O|issn=0022-2488|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Olver|first1=Peter J.|last2=Rosenau|first2=Philip|date=1986-02-10|title=The construction of special solutions to partial differential equations|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0375-9601%2886%2990534-7|journal=Physics Letters A|language=en|volume=114|issue=3|pages=107–112|doi=10.1016/0375-9601(86)90534-7|bibcode=1986PhLA..114..107O|issn=0375-9601|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Olver|first1=Peter J.|last2=Rosenau|first2=Philip|date=1987-04-01|title=Group-Invariant Solutions of Differential Equations|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0147018|journal=SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics|volume=47|issue=2|pages=263–278|doi=10.1137/0147018|issn=0036-1399|url-access=subscription}}</ref> as well as well the theories of [[moving frame]]s and [[Cartan's equivalence method]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fels|first1=Mark|last2=Olver|first2=Peter J.|date=1998-04-01|title=Moving Coframes: I. A Practical Algorithm|url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1005878210297|journal=Acta Applicandae Mathematicae|language=en|volume=51|issue=2|pages=161–213|doi=10.1023/A:1005878210297|s2cid=6681218|issn=1572-9036|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fels|first1=Mark|last2=Olver|first2=Peter J.|date=1999-01-01|title=Moving Coframes: II. Regularization and Theoretical Foundations|url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1006195823000|journal=Acta Applicandae Mathematicae|language=en|volume=55|issue=2|pages=127–208|doi=10.1023/A:1006195823000|s2cid=826629|issn=1572-9036|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[differential invariant]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Olver|first=Peter J.|date=2007-09-01|title=Generating differential invariants|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|series=Special issue dedicated to William Ames|language=en|volume=333|issue=1|pages=450–471|doi=10.1016/j.jmaa.2006.12.029|bibcode=2007JMAA..333..450O|issn=0022-247X|doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[pseudogroup]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Olver|first1=Peter J.|last2=Pohjanpelto|first2=Juha|last3=Valiquette|first3=Francis|date=2009-07-23|title=On the Structure of Lie Pseudo-Groups|url=http://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/2009/077/|journal=SIGMA. Symmetry, Integrability and Geometry: Methods and Applications|language=en|volume=5|pages=077|doi=10.3842/SIGMA.2009.077|arxiv=0907.4086|bibcode=2009SIGMA...5..077O|s2cid=1861888}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Olver|first1=Peter J.|last2=Pohjanpelto|first2=Juha|date=November 2005|title=Maurer–Cartan forms and the structure of Lie pseudo-groups|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00029-005-0008-7|journal=Selecta Mathematica|language=en|volume=11|issue=1|pages=99–126|doi=10.1007/s00029-005-0008-7|s2cid=14712181|issn=1022-1824|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He has written five books and over 150 research papers in peer-reviewed journals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:olver.peter-j|title=Olver, Peter J.|author=zbMATH|access-date=19 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Peter Olver|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=m640mbkAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2021-11-28|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> In 2003, Olver was one of the top 234 most cited mathematicians in the world.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|author=University of Minnesota|title=How do we rank?|url=https://math.umn.edu/news/newsletter/57991#rank|access-date=10 August 2018}}</ref> He has supervised 23 PhD students.<ref name="MGP" /><ref name="CV" />

== Personal life ==
Olver married Iranian mathematician [[Chehrzad Shakiban]] in 1976.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/shakiban.htm|title=Chehrzad Shakiban|work=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|first=Larry|last=Riddle|date=July 2, 2024}}</ref>
